title: The naive cotangent complex of a presentation commutes with localization at one element
statement: Let $A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, $P=A[x_s,\ s\in S]$ a polynomial ring over $A$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] and $\alpha:P\to B$ a surjective homomorphism of $A$-algebras with kernel $I$. For such a presentation write $\mathrm{NL}(\alpha)$ for the two-term complex of $B$-modules $I/I^2\to\Omega_{P/A}\otimes_PB$, $f\bmod I^2\mapsto\mathrm df\otimes1$ ($\Omega$ and $\mathrm d$ as in [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]). Let $g\in B$, let $B_g$ be the localization of $B$ at the powers of $g$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away], choose $f\in P$ with $\alpha(f)=g$, and let $\beta:P[x]\to B_g$ be the homomorphism of $A$-algebras which is $\alpha$ followed by $B\to B_g$ on $P$ and sends the new variable $x$ to $1/g$; let $J=\ker\beta$. Then $\beta$ is surjective, $J$ is generated by $I$ and $fx-1$, and: (1) $J/J^2=(I/I^2)_g\oplus B_g\,(fx-1)$ as $B_g$-modules, where $(I/I^2)_g=I/I^2\otimes_BB_g$ maps to $J/J^2$ by the map induced by $I\subseteq J$, and the second summand is free of rank $1$ on the class of $fx-1$; (2) $\Omega_{P[x]/A}\otimes_{P[x]}B_g=(\Omega_{P/A}\otimes_PB_g)\oplus B_g\,\mathrm dx$; (3) these decompositions can be chosen so that $\mathrm{NL}(\beta)\cong\mathrm{NL}(\alpha)\otimes_BB_g\oplus(B_g\xrightarrow{\ g\ }B_g)$ as complexes of $B_g$-modules. In particular, since $g$ is a unit of $B_g$, the map $(I/I^2)_g\to\Omega_{P/A}\otimes_PB_g$ of $\mathrm{NL}(\alpha)\otimes_BB_g$ is injective if and only if the map $J/J^2\to\Omega_{P[x]/A}\otimes_{P[x]}B_g$ of $\mathrm{NL}(\beta)$ is injective, and the two maps have isomorphic cokernels.

proof.text: For e2 use Mathlib Algebra.Generators.CotangentSpace.compEquiv Q P: the composed cotangent space is Q.CotangentSpace times Bg tensor P.CotangentSpace. Identify Q.CotangentSpace with Bg using its Unit-indexed cotangentSpaceBasis, and exchange the factors. The compEquiv_symm_zero lemma identifies the old summand. The definition of compEquiv through the product basis sends the remaining basis vector to 1 tensor dx. Linearity gives the required e2 inverse formula. Thus no separate polynomial-extension differential theorem is needed.

proof.text: Naturality of the cotangent differential under ofComp shows that the second coordinate of e2(delta_beta[r]) is the Unit coordinate of delta_Q[gx-1]. The cotangentSpaceBasis_repr_one_tmul formula identifies this with evaluation of the partial derivative of gx-1, which is g. Choose the unit u with value g, and let v be the first coordinate of e2(delta_beta[r]). Define k = u inverse times v, and the linear shear t(a,b)=(a+b k,b), with inverse (a,b)=(a-b k,b). Set e0=e2 followed by t inverse. It fixes the old summand and delta_beta[r]=e0 inverse(0,g). Natural compatibility of the base-changed old differential (Mathlib H1Cotangent.map_comp_cotangentComplex_baseChange) and linearity now give delta_beta(e1 inverse(a,b))=e0 inverse(delta_alpha baseChange(a),g b).

proof.text: For the injectivity equivalence, apply e0 to an equality of delta_beta images and express both elements through e1. The resulting equality is (F a,g b)=(F a prime,g b prime). Injectivity of F and cancellation by the unit g imply equality of both coordinates, hence of the original elements. Conversely, injectivity of delta_beta applied to e1 inverse(a,0) and e1 inverse(a prime,0) gives injectivity of F.

proof.text: For cokernels, let q=range F and phi=q.mkQ composed with first projection composed with e0. It is surjective: a representative a of an old quotient class has preimage e0 inverse(a,0). Its kernel is range delta_beta. Indeed phi(x)=0 means the first coordinate of e0 x is F a; if its second coordinate is b, then x=delta_beta(e1 inverse(a,g inverse b)) by the commuting formula. Conversely every delta_beta image maps to zero. Apply LinearMap.quotKerEquivOfSurjective and transport along this equality of submodules, then invert the equivalence to obtain the displayed cokernel isomorphism.
